title: Learning Wisdom For Witnessing From Jesus Part 2
paragraphs: I want you to open your Bibles, if you wish, to the Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Philippians, Chapter Two. Then I want you to write down some phrases. No one was more successful than Jesus in bearing witness to unbelievers. no one. In fact, he was so successful that he warned me. Jesus was able to influence every person in every class of society during his three and a half years of ministry on earth.

This is because God's greatest desire is for every person to return to their original relationship and experience, and to realize their potential in their life. God cares about you more than you care about Him. This includes every single one of the 6. 1 billion people who will be on this planet during the next seven or eight months. The question now is: How did Jesus achieve such remarkable success in preaching? Let me talk a little about the importance of this matter.

We are entering the 21st century, and everyone is talking about the Year 2000 experience. Y stands for year, 2 for 2000, and K for thousand. So, Y2K simply means the year 2000. And everyone is talking about this particular concept, i. e. , moving into a new millennium. As I mentioned earlier, this is also measured against the year 2000 AD. It was named the year 2000 AD because it refers to the year after the death of Christ. Therefore, the millennium is literally measured by the life of Jesus.

However, you won't hear much media talking about Jesus. However, the year 2000 is measured by the life of this great and glorious figure, Jesus Christ. People talk a lot about the Year 2000 problem. They talk about the danger of war, and about the second coming of Christ. The idea of ​​the year 2000 evokes a lot of fear and anxiety. People fear they won't be able to buy gasoline, or that banks will close, or that they won't be able to drive their cars, or that their computers will malfunction.

But everything should revolve around Jesus Christ, for he is the one who determines the millennia. So why is this important to the church? No one should celebrate the coming millennium more than the Church, because it is measured by our Savior and Lord Jesus Christ. The year 2000 also marks the two-thousandth anniversary of the founding of the church. This is a serious matter. This means that the church is two thousand years old.

Two thousand years ago, Jesus founded the Church on the day of Pentecost in Jerusalem, when the Holy Spirit descended and sealed it. Since then, we have begun to measure the birth of the Church. Two thousand years later, the church still stands. It is a very large church, larger than it was at that time. But it was not as effective as it should have been, because it could not grasp Jesus’ wisdom in maximizing the power of the Holy Spirit in guiding the lost.

The last commandment that Jesus gave to the church is found in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 28. We will read it shortly, but its text is as follows: He said to the church: “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to all creation, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and making disciples of all nations.”

In other words, the mission of the Church was to go into the whole world and share the good news of the Kingdom of God, and then to make disciples of every nation, every race, every people, and every community. Our mission, then, was to bring the world back to God. Let me put it very briefly: the Church was not created, then, to go to heaven. The earth was designed to restore God. God cares more about the earth than He cares about heaven. That is why He sent His Son to Earth from Heaven.

Christ was in heaven, but God took him out of it. Because the earth was more important to God than the heavens. Christ died to redeem the earth, not to redeem heaven. Because the earth was more important to God than the heavens. Christ gave his life for sinners on earth, not for angels in heaven. Because the earth is more important to God than the heavens. Then Jesus prayed for the Church not to leave the earth. He said, " Father, do not take them out of the world." Why?

Because the earth is more important to God than the heavens. Heaven belongs to God and is His dominion. But the earth is no longer under God's dominion. God lost this influence with the fall of man. God's response to the fall of man was a promise. A promise to restore man to his original position, which is sovereignty over the earth. Therefore, every human being is in God's mind. The story of the prodigal son is the story of God's will for man.

God saw humanity as a child who left his home and went to waste his life and live with pigs. But remember that God is the Father who still longs for His children to return home. And of course, God sent his son to bring man back to him. God's promise was to become incarnate in the human race and redeem us to Himself. That's his promise. This is what is written in Genesis, Chapter 3:15. Man fell, and God made a promise in verse 15.

The promise was that the offspring of the woman would come and crush your head, Satan, and redeem man for myself. This is what is called salvation. Let us all say the word of salvation. Write the word "salvation" in your notebooks. The first word written under the instructions is salvation. Let us all say the word of salvation. enough. The word "salvation" is derived from the word "to save". Please write that down. enough. enough. The word "salvation" means restoring a person to their original state.

Rescue means restoring something to its original state. The word “ salvation” means God’s plan to restore man to his original state. Now, here's what I want you to grasp in this session: What made Jesus so successful in saving humanity? Why is the Church falling so short in this area? The number of sinners on earth exceeds the number of saints. Today there are more than one billion Muslims, more than 890 million Hindus, and 762 million Shintoists, in addition to believers in multiple gods.

In fact, there are only one billion Christians on Earth, according to statistics. The Earth's population is approximately six billion people. This means that after two thousand years, only one-sixth of the world's population remained Christian. We did not do our job properly. This also means that the birth rate has exceeded the repentance rate. More sinners are born than are born again, because the church has not been able to play its role effectively.

The Earth was smaller, or rather the world was smaller two thousand years ago than it is now, which means we should have been able to attract more people to Christ now, because we would have been more effective on a smaller Earth. Do you understand what I'm saying? The question the Lord asked me in 1998 was, "What are you doing to my church?" So I asked him: "What's the problem with the church?" He said that the church was not effective because it did not understand the message that had been entrusted to us.

How did God try to win the world to Himself? We must study God's plan through Jesus Christ. Look at Isaiah 7:14. He says: “Behold, the Virgin bears a son, and his name is called Emmanuel, which means God with us.” Look at Isaiah 9. Please write that down. Isaiah 9:6 says: “For to us a child is born, and to us what is given?” A son is given to us, and what will his name be? Wonderful, Counselor, Almighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace, whose kingdom has no end. And the presidencies rest on his shoulders.

Repeat after me: And the presidency will be on his shoulders. Once again: the presidency rests on his shoulders. Interesting. The word “sovereignty ” in Genesis 1:26 means “to rule” in Hebrew. God says that through this coming son, God will restore the rule to the earth, and His authority to the earth. But it won't be on his head. Now focus with me. What will it be based on? His shoulders. The Bible says that Christ is the head of the church, and the church is his body. You will understand that soon.

The governing authorities on earth must come from the church. God says that the rule of your nations must rest on the shoulders of Jesus. Who is on his shoulders? The church is his shoulder. We are the body of Christ. This means everyone is saying government. government. Now, the word government in Hebrew also means ruler or authority. It also means manager or leader. This means that every position of authority, government, administration or leadership, must be occupied by a believer.

But the church taught the opposite. The Church taught that we should not assume leadership positions in our countries. We should not assume leadership positions in our businesses. If you become a leader in the business world, you are corrupt. If you have a lot of money, you must be evil. Therefore, the Church preached a message of poverty instead of prosperity. A church that preached a message of slavery instead of rule. A message of submission instead of leadership.

Therefore, the world is the one that runs the church. I mean, who do you work for? For non- believers. These are the people who work. Who is your boss? Often unbeliever. Who pays your salary? Often a non-believer. However, she curses them. The Bible says: The government will be on his shoulders. This means that God's desire is to restore sovereignty over the earth to man through the church. For this reason, we must return to Jesus' system of witnessing. God's program of witnessing begins in this way.

Okay, look at me. I want to show you a short story. It is the story of a man who wanted to understand an ant. He spent many years studying ants. He tried to discover what makes ants so organized, why ants store up in winter, why they walk in straight lines, and why they can build together. He spent years trying to understand that. One day, he had a dream. The dream was that he became an ant too, entered an ant nest, began to understand the language of ants, and began to work with ants.

When he woke up, he clearly understood the world of ants for the first time. He appreciated the feeling of walking on an ant nest. From that day on, he began to protect the ant whenever he saw it. This reminds me of the story of God. God saw the whole earth full of sinners, and He wanted to change them. What did God do? He did not ask sinners to become like him, but rather decided to become like them. In other words, God's program for witnessing is for us to become like those we will bear witness to.

Is n't that clear enough? Now, I want you to read with me the letter of Paul the Apostle to the Philippians, chapter two, to see how God did that. There is no better program than what God has planned, and you cannot improve what God has already set as a program for witnessing. If you are smarter than God, then tell me. I believe we have submitted ourselves to God because He is wiser than us.

Here is God’s program for witnessing: Chapter 2 of the Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Philippians, verse 5: “Let the same mind be in you which was in Christ.” Everyone says: Think. The Bible, in the King James Version, says: " Have the same mind that was in Christ." The NIV translation is more accurate, as it says: "Let the same attitude be in you that was in Christ." In other words, a certain attitude is necessary if you want to bear witness as Jesus bore witness.

Firstly, he who was in the essence of God did not consider his equality with God to be something to be held onto. The Bible, in the King James Version, says: He who found himself equal to God did not regard his equality with God as something to be proud of. This is the main point. The point is that although he was God, he did not feel it necessary to present himself as God. This is very important.

I will repeat this because many Christians do not bear witness because they continue to present themselves as Christians. Oh, my God! As you know, walking around wearing a shirt that says " Jesus Saves" might be a problem rather than a blessing. In fact, if you know Jesus, he may be a distraction rather than an addition. Although he was God, he saw no need to preserve his divinity when he came to Earth. Read the following phrase: "But he emptied himself of all that is important."

The King James Version says: "of every kind." The NIV translation says: " Nothing". He emptied himself of everything. But whose nature did he adopt? What is the nature of a slave created for? In the image of man. What was God trying to do? That humans may win. Jesus, let me explain to you the spirit of this verse. She says he wasn't going around saying, "Do you know who I am? I am God and you all need me. You wicked sinners, I am pure. Don't you know that? You are stained with sin. I am holy. You are unclean.

I am righteous. You are unjust. You had better believe in me." both. Actually, let me tell you something that still amazes me. Jesus allowed three men to see his divinity once. three. He took his three closest friends to a high mountain where no one was. Then he commanded them to be silent, and then suddenly he manifested himself in his divine majesty. His whole body began to glow, his clothes disappeared, and his light and purity appeared, so he became brighter than the sun.

The Bible says it was so bright that it outshone the daytime sun. They saw God. Follow me. When they saw him, their response was: "Let's stay here." This is like me. Let's stay here. This is a good act of worship, my brother. Let us remain in the presence of the Lord. There are people in the neighborhoods who are dying and going to hell. Peter says, "Let us build three tents." This means three houses. A tent means a house. Peter did not want to return to his wife. Let me tell you something.

No matter how strong you become, go back to your home, to your husband. Go back to your home, to your wife. When the service is over, go back to your home and be your wife. Be your husband. Go ahead, clap here. Go back home and be what you're supposed to be. Peter wanted to move and build a new house after this great miracle. Listen to the words of Jesus. You might think that the important words are those in which he said: “This is my beloved son, listen to him.”

But the most important words that amazed me were his words: "Don't tell anyone." Oh my God, Jesus! What? We just saw it! We must tell everyone. He says, "Don't tell anyone, not even after my resurrection." We have just seen God. He said, "That's true. And I don't want anyone to see me as a god." Hey everyone, are you with me? Let me explain to you how this relates to you. You enter a place. Praise the Lord. Hallelujah. Oh my God, be quiet. This is a language foreign to sinners.

They are supposed to discover that you are born again, filled with the Holy Spirit, baptized, believers speaking in tongues, when it is too late. I am trying to explain why there are more sinners than saints after two thousand years. We continue to remove sinners. Why? Because we continue—unwillingly—to believe that clinging to the image of a religious person is more important than becoming like the person we are trying to talk to. Do you know why sinners avoid us? Because we make them feel like sinners.

He did not make any reputation for himself. Oh my God, here she comes again. Oh my God, she can talk about Jesus again. I know her reputation. Yes, here he comes again. He is extremely talkative. Everything revolves around Jesus. Jesus, Jesus, Jesus. Let's go. What is your reputation? Young people, you must know that what distinguishes you is what you do not do. There should be no loud talk or high-pitched speeches about being Christians and saints, or speaking publicly about how God saved you.

Rather, they should see you living. Read the following line. Did everyone understand this? Verse seven. He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in human likeness, being made in appearance like what? man. What did he do? He humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore, God exalted him and gave him a name above every name. That every knee should bow at the name of Jesus Christ, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

God says, "I love my son." Because he did not try to be holier than others. He knew how to testify. Look at this statement. It amazes me. To exist in human form. This is amazing. This is God, my friends. This is God. This is Elohim, Adonai, El Shari, Yahweh Rapha, Yahweh Shescanu. This is Jehovah Nissi. This is the great and glorious one of the world. It comes in human form. I think this is so amazing it's hard to believe. That's why they didn't believe him.

As you know, people are supposed to think that you are not a Christian. But do you know why? Because you are in the room where they are smoking and the smoke surrounds your face and you are still smiling. How can you be a Christian with all this alcohol around you? The answer should be: Because I am in the world. I look like you, but I'm not really. Come on, people. I have the appearance of a man, but I am from a different kingdom. Let me tell you something. I discovered something. Lord, help me.

Look, I need to understand this. If your Christianity cannot withstand an environment of sinners, then you do not have a true Christianity. If you need a Christianity protected by church doors and stained-glass sellers, then you don't have real Christianity. Come on, everyone. If it is real, it is supposed to influence the world, not the other way around. Christ was not afraid of sinners. Why? Because it was the cure. Have you ever seen a medicine run away from the disease? He was in human form.

Let me show you something interesting. You will be blessed. Open the Gospel of John, chapter three. The Gospel of John, Chapter Three. A very familiar verse. Verse 16. Please open there. Please take your pen. Underline this verse. Read it for the first time, then read it again. The Gospel of John, Chapter 3, Verse 15, Verse 16. Out loud together. For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not be killed. He shall not perish, but shall have eternal life.

Read verse 13. No one ever went, out loud please. No one has ever gone into heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man. Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life. Now read verse 16. For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. Read verse 17, which is the most important verse.

Because God did not send his son into the world to tell the world about their evil deeds. We are now very good at that. Because God did not send his son into the world for any purpose? To condemn the world, but to save the world through him. Wow! I wonder how people feel when they meet you as a Christian. We are talking about the New Millennium Church. We need change. I heard the Holy Spirit say to me, "We have to change. We cannot continue like this."

But the problem is that we have n't been trained to do it any other way. That is why this entire series is extremely important. God teaches us how to change our way of thinking, even in our lives. People are bored with us as Christians. We condemn them. Christ was a wonderful example of martyrdom. Everyone loved him. The prostitutes loved him. The beggars loved him. He was loved by alcoholics. Refer to the Gospel of Luke, chapter five. The Gospel of Luke, Chapter 5. Tell your neighbors: I must change.

Tell your neighbors: I am blocking the road. I am blocking the way. There are people who want salvation. We know that from our previous sessions. The Bible says that the harvest is what? mature. It is not ready to mature. It's already ripe. It has been like this for two thousand years. So, the problem isn't with the harvest. There is something wrong with the workers. Jesus said that we should pray for more experienced, mature, and skilled workers.

But if the workers cannot complete the harvesting task, we waste the crop. Luke 5:30 is a wonderful verse. She says, "Let's understand the context." Let's understand the context now. Let's understand the context. Let's read the context. What is the context? The previous verses, right? So, let's understand the context of the verse. Verse 30. We begin with verse 27. After that, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting in the tax collection place. Jesus said to him: Follow me.

So Levi got up, left everything, and followed him. Then Levi held a great feast for Jesus in his house. Oh, my God. Now, the tax collector in Jesus' time was more like a customs officer. Who was forcing you to pay? Who was searching everything? We are now talking to the Bohemians. They force you to take off your socks and handkerchief, find your belongings, and force you to pay an exorbitant amount. They tell you that you will not leave the airport until you pay. And she gets angry with them.

Then Jesus comes from the row right behind you and says, "I want you to have dinner with me, customs officer." And you are listening to this. Do you understand the idea? Yes. That's what Matta was like. Matta was an accountant at the customs office. People were forced to pay taxes through their bonds. He forced them to pay customs duties. They didn't like him any more than you like a customs officer. Come on, sit up straight. You are more like bohemians.

When you arrive at the airport or the ship terminal, you feel nervous. Why? You see those white collared shirts and those black trousers. You feel stressed. Why? You hate these men and women. Why? They come to collect your customs duties. Why don't you like them? Now, are they stealing from you? no. Matt was not a thief. We still call Matthew the thief. He was a customs officer. Do you know why you hate customs officers? They are taking the money that you are supposed to pay. But why don't you like them?

Because you don't want to pay. That's why they hated tax collectors. It was a culturally ingrained hatred, as in the Bahamas. I mean, some of you want to be friendly with these people so that they will be lenient with you. Matthew was the one who wasn't friendly. You smiled, so he smiled back and opened everything. He forced you to open it while smiling. They didn't like him because he forced them to pay taxes. You are smiling. You must understand what I mean. Some of you look guilty. Good. So, this was Matthew.

Matthew was that person at the job. They didn't like that. In verse 30 of the Book of Jesus, the Levites, that is, those who were eating with Jesus in Matthew’s house, were being complained about by the Pharisees and teachers of the law of their sect to his disciples, saying: “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?” Wow! That's amazing! We describe customs officials as sinners; they work for the government and collect your taxes.

Their question about Jesus and his disciples was: " Why do you associate with sinners?" Read the answer. Jesus answered, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance." Let me explain it in another way. He says: Look, if I go to your house and you say that you are righteous, then I am not doing my job. Oh, you missed this. He said, "Look, if there is someone you want to win for the kingdom of God, invite him to your house for dinner."

Can you imagine giving a ride to a homeless person? Even better, you should go to his house. "Yes. Jesus said, 'I did not come to save the righteous.'" That's why I won't come to your house. I came to save sinners. That's why I'm going to his house. I have named him wrong, and these are the ones I came to save. So, I will go to his house. "Look at chapter seven on the opposite page. Chapter seven, verse 34. The context. Verse 33. John the Baptist came neither eating nor drinking wine.

I found the context here interesting. I read this the other day. And I said, ' Man, this is amazing.'" He says: "John the Baptist came, what?" He neither eats nor drinks alcohol. "And what do you say? That he's possessed by a demon. Do you understand this? He says that if I don't drink and smoke, you'll say I'm possessed by a demon. Now read the following passage. The Son of Man, that is, Jesus, came to eat and drink. And you say he was rude, a drunkard, and a friend of tax collectors and sinners.

But wisdom proves itself through all its children. Well, I'm going to start preaching now. That's what we're going to address here. We're going to settle this here. First, he says that religious people are crazy. He says, and let me paraphrase him: 'First, if you do good, they complain.'" And if you don't do good, they complain. What do these people want? He says: "What do you want?" "Let me tell you something, even if you don't mix with sinners now, they will still think that you are not among the faithful.

That's what he says. He said: " John the Baptist did not drink, nor did he eat with these sick people, yet they still call him the devil." He said: "Now I will come, eat with him, and drink with him." And you describe me as greedy and sinful? Then he said, " Okay, what do you want?" "Oh, how strange!" Then he made a strong statement. He said, " Wisdom!" Let everyone say: Wisdom! "Oh, that's great." Say: Wisdom! "Wisdom. I want you to write down three words, please. The first word: knowledge.

The second word: understanding. The third word: wisdom. What's the difference? First, knowledge is information. Understanding is revelation. Wisdom is application. I want you to understand this well. Don't miss this revelation. Knowledge is what? I ca n't hear you. Information. When God gives you information, you gain knowledge. That's what teaching does. That's what God's word gives you when you read it. That's what God gives you when you hear God's word being taught. You gain information. That's knowledge.

You know the word. But then you move to the second step, and what is it? Understanding, and what is it? Revelation. This means you receive revelation of information. You understand what you heard. You have understood it. But that's not enough. You have to move to the final stage, and what is it? Wisdom, which is application. He says that your problem, Pharisees and scribes, is that you have received information, and some of you have received revelation, but you don't have application.

You can't apply the word you learn to..." Sinners. You know, there's something the Lord told me clearly in November. He says that a 21st-century church must be a four-word church. First, what is that word? Wisdom, then skill, then diplomacy, then application. A church that can take what it knows about the Kingdom and apply it to its current work. This requires wisdom. Jesus said, " What you see me doing now is wisdom." Do you understand? They said, "You eat with these sinners and keep company with drunkards."

You associate with prostitutes. What do you do? He said, “This is wisdom.” Do n’t you see wisdom? A child, a child of wisdom, does this. A child of wisdom applies information. He knows how to make it effective in daily life. Reaching the world and bringing it back to God was Jesus’ clear mission and his clear commission to the church. Jesus’ first concern and greatest passion was to lead all people to God. This is what Jesus wanted.

That is why he says in John 4:34, “My food is to do the will of my Father who sent me.” And in verse 35, he says, “Do not say, ‘It is five months until harvest.’ I tell you, lift up your eyes and see that the fields are ripe for harvest.” Don’t you see? He says, “So, one sows and another reaps. I sent you to reap what you did not labor for. Others labored, and you reaped the fruits of their labor.” He says, “I have already done all the fertilizing.” I have prepared the harvest for you.

Go forth and reap what you did not sow. It is easy, he says, to win over the lost. But the church failed in that. The Church fulfills its purpose and mission when it reaches the world. Allow me to make a statement here. Please, please, please understand the context of this. For the past seven or eight months I have been praying, pleading with God and saying: Lord, what is the problem with the church in the world?

This means not only taking responsibility here in this ministry, but also includes the other churches that I have to go to for help. The Holy Spirit told me that the reason for the weakness and sickness of the Church was that it was only blessing itself. We are so concerned with what we gain that we have forgotten our brother who is suffering. We've become the big brother in the house. The person who is upset because the older brother who came is giving the country some attention.

I am thinking of those who call people to repentance, for example. What do you do when people rise up to accept Christ? You look at your watch. It's time to go home. In other words, this "big brother" mentality means: there's nothing for me there. There's nothing for me there. There's nothing for me there. Then you end up attacking the group. It begins by attacking the group because its goal is to reach those who have gone astray. But when you have no vision for the lost, you begin to attack and destroy yourself.

Therefore, Jesus said, "The harvest is ripe." " Look at him." He says, “ I have sent you to reap what you have not sown. I have prepared this field for you. Go and reap.” Over the years, the Church has repeatedly blamed the world itself for its failure to reach the world effectively. Did you understand what I said? How many times have you said, "I know I said it, I tried to testify to you and you don't want to be saved. That's your business. Go to hell. Go on. You said it.

I've been talking to you about God for the last ten years. Dad, if you don't want to be saved, that's your business. Go to hell. Mom, I've been talking. Sister and brother, I've been talking to you for years. Cousin, I've been talking to you. Teacher, I've been talking to you. Brother, I've been..." We are angry with them because they do not want to be saved. Now, we have a problem here. Jesus said they were mature. You say they are stubborn, they are immature. Jesus said they were ready. You say they are cruel.

Christ said they are eggs for the harvest. This means they have already bent down. They are rotten. To be chosen. He said, "But you tell them that you are stubborn." Is it conceivable that we don't know how to choose them? Have you ever considered that the problem might lie with you, not with the culprit? Listen again to the word of God from the Book of Proverbs. Winning over a humiliated brother is harder than winning over a walled city. You want to win the person over.

God says, "Then do not do anything wrong to him." Now we call people's abuse persecution. We say: "Well, the reason you resist God is that you are filled with the devil." No, not the devil. You have wronged me. You made me feel inferior. nothing. You may feel like you are wrong, like you are a bad person. You think you're better than me. That's why I don't want to listen to you. That's what the wrongdoer says. But Jesus, what kind of man is this? The prostitutes were looking for him. The vagrants sought him out.

The poor loved his presence. The thieves enjoyed his company. Sinners loved to drink with him. How could they love him and not love us? We are the religious ones. We caught her in adultery, and the law said kill her. It is religion. You smoke, you drink, you die, you go to hell. That's what the law says. Jesus says, "Which of you is without sin?" Go ahead, start the stoning. What kind of man is this? He loves sinners. They have wronged this woman with what they said. The law says it is the woman's womb.

Where are those who accused you? I am not accusing you. Wow! The Church has made the world responsible for its own failure. The world has told us that the reason you are not saved is because you do not want to be saved. Jesus said, "No, the world is not saved because you did not know how to save it." There is a huge difference. Let me point out here that Jesus was very successful in reaching the world effectively, and his difficulty was limited to the religious.

Strangely enough, it reached all levels of society, regardless of gender, class, or race. He was able to transcend both gender, race, and class with ease. He captured everyone's attention. He instructed us to do the same. In Matthew 28:18, please open there quickly. In Matthew 28:18, he says these words in the Gospel of Matthew, and it is a powerful statement. We've all read it before. I want you to see it written down. I want to underline two words. That's why I want you to find it. Matthew, chapter 28.

Everyone, please open up. Young people, read this. This is the mission that God has given you as young Christians as well. Viewers of this television program, if you are believers, this is your responsibility. I will read now.
